Theme

Household, washing & chores

iron verb and noun

for clothes

also ironing, iron clothes, press clothes

modern

Traupman 334
M-O s.v. iron (clothes)

lēvigō, lēvigāre

verb, first conjugation

smooth, iron

From lēvis, smooth; classical in the sense “smooth”. No source gives an ironing board.

Other words

  • ferrum — an iron

    modern · M-O s.v. iron (clothes)

    Morgan–Owens: an iron is simply ferrum.

  • vestīmenta premere — iron clothes

    also used · modern · Traupman 38; Traupman 334

  • prēlum — a clothes-press

    also used · classical · Mart. 2.46.3: tua collūcent prēla lacernīs (Lewis & Short)

    Martial’s clothes-press.

Examples

  • Cavē! Ferrum calidum est.

    Careful! The iron is hot.composed

See also laundry, fold.

SourcesLewis & Short: premo · Lewis & Short: levigo · Lewis & Short: prelum

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. laundry (place to wash clothes), laundry: do the laundry, iron (clothes), soap: laundry detergent, laundry: dry cleaner’s. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 38, 123, 124, 303, 307, 317, 334, 338, 404.

Cicero from the Latinitas loci collection; Laberius and Martial as cited by L&S.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
